examples.dm: One who does not apprehend the supreme perfection of wisdom, Does not apprehend the bodhisattva, and does not apprehend the mind of awakening; Upon hearing this, one who is not bewildered and has no fear, That bodhisattva practices the wisdom of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: One who does not apprehend the supreme perfection of wisdom, Does not apprehend the bodhisattva, and does not apprehend the mind of awakening; Having heard this, the one who is without delusion and without fear, That bodhisattva practices the wisdom of the Sugata.
examples.sa: यस्मिन् न प्रज्ञवरपारमितोपलब्धिः न च बोधिसत्त्व-उपलब्धि न चित्तबोधेः । एवं श्रुणित्व न च मुह्यति नास्ति त्रासो सो बोधिसत्त्व चरते सुगतान प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: These beings are stuck in the mire of name and form; They wander in the wheel of cyclic existence, which is like a wheel driven by wind. Knowing that deluded beings are like deer caught in a snare, Those endowed with wisdom move through the sky like birds.
examples.gm: These wandering beings are attached to the mud of name and form; They wander in the wheel of samsara like a wheel of wind. Knowing that deluded beings are like deer caught in a snare, The wise one roams like a bird in the sky.
examples.sa: नामेव रूपि जगती अयु पङ्कसक्ता संसारचक्रि भ्रमतेऽनिलचक्रतुल्ये । जानित्व भ्रान्तु जगती मृगवागुरेव आकाश पक्षिसदृशा विचरन्ति प्रज्ञाः ॥

examples.dm: When a mother falls ill, though she has many children, They all become distressed and perform healing rites for her. In the same way, the Buddhas of the world systems in the ten directions Direct their intention toward this supreme Perfection of Wisdom, who is their mother.
examples.gm: When a mother becomes sick and has many sons, They all become unhappy and attend upon her. Likewise, the Buddhas of the world systems in the ten directions also Keep in mind this holy wisdom, which is their mother.
examples.sa: मात्राय पुत्र बहु सन्ति गिलानि काये ते सर्वि दुर्मनस तत्र प्रयुज्ययेयुः । एमेव बुद्धपिं दशद्दिशि लोकधातौ इम प्रज्ञपारमित मात्र समन्वाहरन्ति ॥

examples.dm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness; One does not dwell in the attainment of the fruit or the stage of an arhat, Nor does one dwell in the stage of a pratyekabuddha or likewise the stage of a buddha.
examples.gm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, attractive and unattractive, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness, Attaining the fruit, and not abiding in the level of an arhat, Not abiding in the level of a pratyekabuddha, and likewise not in the level of a buddha.
examples.sa: नित्यम् अनित्यसुखदुःखशुभाशुभं ति आत्मन्य् अनात्मि तथता तथ शून्यतायाम् । फलप्राप्तिताय अथितो अरहन्तभूमौ प्रत्येकभूमिस्थितो तथ बुद्धभूमौ ॥

examples.dm: Why is that? Because those supreme speakers, having trained in this, Here demonstrate that all phenomena are emptiness. Having heard that, the Hearers quickly reach liberation, And they reach the awakening of Pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of Buddhas.
examples.gm: If asked why: those supreme speakers, having trained in this, Demonstrate all dharmas here as emptiness. Hearing that, śrāvakas swiftly touch complete liberation, And touch the awakening of pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of buddhas.
examples.sa: किं कारणं त इह शिक्षित वादिश्रेष्ठा गमयन्ति धर्म निखिलानिह शून्यतायाम् । यां श्रुत्व श्रावक स्पृशन्ति विमुक्ति शीघ्रं प्रत्येकबोधि स्पृशयन्ति च बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Except for those who constantly dwell in villages, regions, and towns, Striving for awakening and the ripening of sentient beings, And who do not generate the desire for the state of an Arhat or Pratyekabuddha— This is what the Sugata calls the solitude of the [Buddha's] sons.
examples.gm: Constantly abiding in villages, provinces, and towns, Except for striving for awakening to mature sentient beings, They do not produce other desires for arhatship or pratyekabuddhahood; This is taught by the sons of the Sugata as being solitary.
examples.sa: ग्रामे च राष्ट्रि निगमे विहरन्ति नित्यं रहप्रत्ययानि स्पृहतां जनयन्ति तत्र । अन्यत्र सत्त्वपरिपाचनबोधियुक्ता एषो विवेकु कथितो सुगतात्मजानाम् ॥

examples.dm: One who does not practice in form, feeling, perception, or intention, And does not practice in consciousness, practices without a fixed abode. Not apprehending the thought "I am practicing," such a one relies on wisdom; The unborn and intelligent touch the supreme peace of meditative stabilization.
examples.gm: Whoever does not practice regarding form, feeling, perception, or volition, And does not practice regarding consciousness, practices without dwelling. Not apprehending what is called "practicing," they rely on wisdom. Possessing the intelligence of the unborn, they contact the supreme, peaceful samādhi.
examples.sa: न च रुप वेदन न संज्ञ न चेतनाया विज्ञानि यो न चरती अनिकेतचारी । चरतीति सो न उपगच्छति प्रज्ञधारी अनुपादधी स्पृशति शान्ति समाधि श्रेष्ठाम् ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the skillful bodhisattva also, Generates great compassion for all realms of sentient beings, And having completely transcended the four Māras and even the two levels, Abides in supreme meditative absorption, yet does not touch upon awakening.
examples.gm: Likewise, at that time, a skilled bodhisattva, Generating great compassion for all realms of sentient beings, Having utterly passed beyond the four māras and the two, Dwells in the supreme samādhi and does not touch awakening.
examples.sa: एमेव यस्मि समये विदु बोधिसत्त्वो महमैत्रि सर्वि उपबन्धति सत्त्वधातौ । चतुरो स मार अतिक्रम्य द्वये च भूमिम् अस्मिन् समाधि स्थितु नो च स्पृशाति बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: When a bodhisattva who is wise and clear-minded Practices this supreme samadhi of empty peace, During that time, one does not cultivate any signs; Abiding in the signless, one practices peace and utter tranquility.
examples.gm: Whenever a skilled and brilliant bodhisattva Engages in this supreme samādhi of peaceful emptiness, During that time they do not intensely cultivate signs; Dwelling in signlessness, they practice peace and profound peace.
examples.sa: यस्मिंश् च कालि विदु पण्डितु बोधिसत्त्वो चरती इमां प्रवर शून्य समाधि शान्ताम् । अत्रान्तरे न च निमित्त प्रभावितव्यो न च आनिमित्तस्थितु शान्त प्रशान्तचारी ॥

examples.dm: Those who think, "May I become a disciple of the Sugata," And those who desire to become Pratyekabuddhas or likewise Kings of Dharma, Cannot achieve these without relying on this patience, Just as one cannot cross from this shore to the other without seeing the ferry.
examples.gm: Whoever thinks they will become a śrāvaka of the Sugata, Or a pratyekabuddha, and likewise wishes to become a Dharma King, Cannot attain it without relying on this patience, Just as one cannot see a crossing to go from this shore to the other.
examples.sa: यो इच्छती सुगतश्रावक हं भवेयं प्रत्येकबुद्ध भवियां तथ धर्मराजो । इमु क्षान्त्यनागमि न शक्यति प्रापुणेतुं यथ आरपारगमनाय अतीतदर्शी ॥

examples.dm: Whips, sticks, weapons, being killed, bound, or beaten, Decapitation, and the cutting off of ears, feet, hands, and nose— Thinking, "I shall endure whatever worldly sufferings there may be," The bodhisattva abides in the perfection of patience.
examples.gm: "Whips, sticks, weapons, killing, binding, and beating, Severing of the head, and cutting off ears, hands, feet, and nose— Whatever sufferings exist in the world, I will endure them!" Thinking this, the bodhisattva abides in the perfection of patience.
examples.sa: कशदण्डशस्त्रवधबन्धनताडनाश्च शिरछेदकर्णचरणाकरनासछेदाः । यावन्ति दुःख जगती अहु तत्सहामि क्षान्तीय पारमित तिष्ठति बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: If they should hear others speaking ill or using harsh words, The wise bodhisattva rejoices, thinking, "This is my happiness." Who speaks, who hears, who [speaks] to whom, and for what reason? One who possesses this supreme perfection of patience is wise.
examples.gm: If one hears abusive and harsh words from others, Thinking, "I am happy," the wise bodhisattva rejoices; Who speaks, who hears, by what, what is it, and for what reason? The wise one is endowed with the supreme perfection of patience.
examples.sa: परुषं श्रुणित्व वचनं परतो दुरुक्तं परितोषयाति सुसुखं विदु बोधिसत्त्वो । को भाषते क शृणुते कुतु कस्य केन सो युक्त क्षान्तिवरपारमिताय विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom
examples.gm: The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom

examples.dm: In the language of India: Ārya-prajñāpāramitā-sañcayagāthā. In the language of Tibet: 'Phags pa shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa sdud pa tshigs su bcad pa. Homage to the Noble Mañjuśrī!
examples.gm: In the language of India: Āryaprajñāpāramitāsañcayagāthā. In the language of Tibet: The Noble Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom. Homage to the noble Mañjuśrī.
examples.sa: ओम् नमो भगवत्यै आर्यप्रज्ञापारमितारत्नगुणसंचयगाथायै । नमो आर्यमञ्जुश्रिये ।

examples.dm: The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: The Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom
examples.sa: रत्नगुणसंचयगाथा ।

examples.dm: Suppose someone were to make offerings to the stūpas Of the Sugatas who have passed into parinirvāṇa, constructing them of the seven precious gems, And were to fill a thousand million buddha-fields With as many stūpas of the Sugatas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges;
examples.gm: If someone, of the completely parinirvāṇized Sugata, Were to build stūpas from the seven precious things and make offerings, and with those stūpas of the Sugata, as numerous as the Ganges' Sands, were to fill thousands of millions of fields;
examples.sa: परिनिर्वृतस्य सुगतस्य करेय्य स्तूपां पूजेय सप्तरतनामयु कश्चिद् एव । तेहि प्रपूर्ण सिय क्षेत्रसहस्रकोट्यो यथ गङ्गवालिकसमैः सुगतस्य स्तूपैः ॥

examples.dm: If in infinite tens of millions of realms, All the sentient beings who dwell therein, Were to do nothing else but offer divine flowers, the finest incense, And ointments for three eons or even longer,
examples.gm: And if, in infinite millions of fully conceived fields, All of the sentient beings, however many reside there, Doing no other work, with divine flowers, supreme incense, and Ointments, were to make offerings for aeons of the three times or even more—
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व पुन तान्तक क्षेत्रकोट्यो ते सर्वि पूजन करेयुर् अनन्तकल्पान् । दिव्येहि पुष्पवरगन्धविलेपनेहि कल्पांस् त्रियध्वपरिकल्प ततोऽपि भूयः ॥

examples.dm: The Victor, having been asked a question by Śakra, replied: If there were Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, And all of them were filled to the brim with the relics of the Victors, I would still take this very Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: The Victor fully asked Śakra a question, and he replied: "Even if there were buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, And all of them were filled to the brim with the relics of the Victors, I would take this very perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: शक्रो जिनेन परिपृच्छितु प्रश्नमाहु सचि गङ्गवालिकसमा सिय बुद्धक्षेत्राः । जिनधातु सर्वि परिपूरित चूडिबद्धा इमम् एव प्रज्ञवरपारमिताहु गृह्णे ॥

examples.dm: Just as the Guide does not dwell in the unconditioned realm, Likewise, one does not dwell in the conditioned, but practices without a fixed location; In that way, the bodhisattva dwells by not dwelling in any basis; To dwell without a location is what the Victor has taught as "dwelling."
examples.gm: Just as the Guide does not abide in the unconditioned realm, Likewise not abiding in the conditioned, practicing without abiding; Thus the bodhisattva abides in an abiding that is without abiding; Abiding without abiding, this is taught as abiding by the Victorious One.
examples.sa: यथ नायकोऽस्थितकु धातुअसंस्कृताया तथ संस्कृताय अथितो अनिकेतचारी । एवं च स्थानु अथितो स्थित बोधिसत्त्वो अस्थानु स्थानु अयु स्थानु जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Those who engage in the practice of benefit and compassion, Having trained in this vidyā-mantra, the wise shall touch enlightenment; One should know that all forms of happiness, Whether conditioned or unconditioned, arise from this.
examples.gm: Those who practice the practices endowed with benefit and compassion, The wise ones, having trained in this mantra, will touch awakening. Whatever is conditioned happiness and unconditioned happiness, One should know that all those forms of happiness arise from this.
examples.sa: ये वा चरन्ति चरियां हितसानुकम्पाम् इह विद्यशिक्षित विदु स्पृशिष्यन्ति बोधिम् । ये सौख्य संस्कृत असंस्कृत ये च सौख्या सर्वे च सौख्य प्रसुता इतु वेदितव्याः ॥

examples.dm: When conditioned and unconditioned phenomena, as well as white and black dharmas, Have been thoroughly deconstructed by wisdom so that not even an atom is observed, That is accounted as the perfection of wisdom in the world; It is just like space, which does not abide in anything at all.
examples.gm: When conditioned, unconditioned, and white and black dharmas Are broken down by wisdom and not even a particle is apprehended, In the world it is reckoned as the perfection of wisdom; It is like space, which does not abide anywhere at all.
examples.sa: यद धर्म संस्कृत असंस्कृत कृष्णशुक्लो अणुमात्रु नो लभति प्रज्ञ विभावमानः । यद प्रज्ञपारमित गच्छति संख्य लोके आकाश यत्र न प्रतिष्ठितु किंचि तत्र ॥

examples.dm: The Perfection of Wisdom is the pleasure grove where they abide; It is the sphere of activity for the Guides who possess the ten powers. Although they completely deliver sentient beings from the sufferings of the three lower realms, They never entertain the notion of a "sentient being."
examples.gm: Relying on the perfection of wisdom as a pleasure grove, This is the domain of the guides with the ten powers; Even though they fully extract sentient beings from the suffering of the three lower realms, They never have the notion of "sentient beings".
examples.sa: अयु गोचरो दशबलान विनायकानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित रम्यवनाश्रितानाम् । दुखितांश्च सत्त्व त्रिअपाय समुद्धरन्ति न पि सत्त्वसंज्ञ अपि तेषु कदाचि भोति ॥

examples.dm: They are free from the perception of diversity and speak words consistent with reason; They do not rely on other śramaṇas or brahmins. These wise ones have forever abandoned the three lower realms; They are intensely devoted to the paths of the ten virtuous actions.
examples.gm: Free from differentiated perceptions and speaking rational words, Not relying on other śramaṇas and brahmins; The wise always abandon the three lower realms at all times, And vividly strive in the path of the ten virtuous actions.
examples.sa: नानात्वसंज्ञविगता गिर युक्तभाणी न च अन्य ते श्रमण ब्राह्मण आश्रयन्ति । त्रियपायवर्जित विदू सदकालि भोन्ति दशभिश् च ते कुशलकर्मपथेभि युक्ता ॥

examples.dm: If, in a dream, one sees sentient beings dwelling in the three lower realms, And in that very moment makes a prayer to cut the continuum of the lower realms, And pacifies a mass of fire through the power of the blessing of truth— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: In a dream, seeing sentient beings abiding in the three lower realms, In that instant they make aspirations to cut off the stream of the lower realms. Through the blessing of truth, the masses of fire are pacified; They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: त्रि-अपायप्राप्तु सुपिनस्मि विदित्व सत्त्वान् प्रणिधेति तत्क्षण अपाय उच्छोषयेयम् । सत्याधिष्ठानि प्रशमेति स चाग्निस्कन्धम् अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यो ॥

examples.dm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness; One does not dwell in the attainment of the fruit or the stage of an arhat, Nor does one dwell in the stage of a pratyekabuddha or likewise the stage of a buddha.
examples.gm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, attractive and unattractive, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness, Attaining the fruit, and not abiding in the level of an arhat, Not abiding in the level of a pratyekabuddha, and likewise not in the level of a buddha.
examples.sa: नित्यम् अनित्यसुखदुःखशुभाशुभं ति आत्मन्य् अनात्मि तथता तथ शून्यतायाम् । फलप्राप्तिताय अथितो अरहन्तभूमौ प्रत्येकभूमिस्थितो तथ बुद्धभूमौ ॥

examples.dm: The teaching of the Dharma, the listening, and whatever is taught, The attainment of the result, the Pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the clarity of the wise— The Tathāgata has taught that all these are like an illusion.
examples.gm: The one who teaches the Dharma, the one who listens, and whatever is to be taught, The attainment of the fruit, the pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the brilliant wise ones— All these are taught by the Tathāgata to be like an illusion.
examples.sa: यो धर्म भाष्यति य भाष्यति भाष्यमाणां फलप्राप्त प्रत्ययजिनो तथ लोकनाथो । निर्वाणतो अधिगतो विदुपण्डितेहि सर्वे त आत्मज निदृष्ट तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: One should understand that the purity of form is the purity of the fruition; The purity of the fruition and the purity of form become the purity of omniscience. The purity of omniscience, the purity of the fruition, and the purity of form Are like the element of space—indivisible and inseparable.
examples.gm: The purity of form should be known as the purity of the fruit; The purity of the fruit and form becomes the purity of omniscience. The purity of omniscience, the purity of the fruit, and the purity of form Are equal to the realm of space, indivisible and unseverable.
examples.sa: रूपस्य शुद्धि फलशुद्धित वेदितव्या फलरूपशुद्धित सर्वज्ञतशुद्धिम् आहुः । सर्वज्ञताय फलशुद्धित रूपशुद्धी आकाशधातुसमताय अभिन्नछिन्नाः ॥

examples.dm: Yogis who practice the supreme Perfection of Wisdom, Do not see any increase or decrease in form. One who does not see phenomena, non-phenomena, or the sphere of phenomena, And does not touch nirvana, is established in wisdom.
examples.gm: When practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom, the yogi Does not see the increase or complete decrease of form; Whoever does not see dharma, non-dharma, or the dharmadhātu, And does not touch nirvāṇa, they abide in wisdom.
examples.sa: चरमाणु प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय योगी न च रूपवृद्धि न च पश्यति पारिहाणिम् । धर्मा अधर्म इमु पश्यति धर्मधातुं न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति सो विहराति प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: It does not abide within the dharmadhātu or suchness; For example, like a cloud in the sky, it abides without a place to abide. A mantra-holder, a sky-traveler without a fixed abode, desiring a place to stay, Through the power of mantra, blesses trees to be endowed with out-of-season flowers.
examples.gm: They do not dwell in the dharmadhātu or suchness, For example, like clouds in space, they dwell without dwelling. A mantra-holder, without a dwelling, moving in space, wishing to dwell, By the power of mantras, is endowed with out-of-season flowers and blesses them.
examples.sa: न च धर्मधातुतथताय उपैति स्थानं भवती अथानस्थित सो लघु अन्तरीक्षे । विद्याधरो व अभिलम्भु वनाभिप्राया खगु कालहीन द्रुम मन्त्रबलाधिष्ठानो ॥

examples.dm: This is the supreme treasure of Dharma and the most excellent Dharma treasury; It is the Buddha lineage, the treasury of happiness and joy for all beings. The protectors of the world in the ten directions—those of the past and those yet to come— All arise from this, yet the expanse of reality is never exhausted.
examples.gm: This is the supreme Dharma-treasure and the holy Dharma-treasury; It is the lineage of the Buddhas, the treasury of happiness and joy of beings. The protectors of the world of the past, future, and the ten directions, Though they are born from this, the dharmadhātu does not become exhausted.
examples.sa: अग्रं निधान अयु उत्तमधर्मकोश बुद्धान गोत्रजननं सुखसौख्यगञ्जो । अतिक्रान्तनागत दशद्दिशि लोकनाथा इतु ते प्रसूत न च क्षीयति धर्मधातुः ॥

examples.dm: In this way, those who have entered supreme enlightenment should never abandon The yoga of the perfection of wisdom, which is like a precious jewel. Just as one who finds a jewel, takes it up, and wraps it with great care, Will quickly travel on and reach a state of peace.
examples.gm: Likewise, one entered into supreme awakening should not abandon yoga In the jewel-like perfection of wisdom; Having found and taken the jewel, one should thoroughly apply exertion, Swiftly progressing, just as one becomes pacified.
examples.sa: एमेव बोधिवरप्रस्थित रत्नतुल्यो प्रज्ञाय पारमित योगु न रिञ्चितव्यो । रतनं व लब्ध्व गृहमाणु अभिन्नसत्त्वो अनुबुद्धयति त्वरितो शिवमभ्युपैति ॥

examples.dm: Through ethical discipline, those who desire peace become noble. Abiding in the domain of the ten powers, their ethical discipline never declines. They follow all the various activities of the vows; For the benefit of all beings, they also dedicate them to enlightenment.
examples.gm: Through discipline, those who desire peace become exalted; Abiding in the domain of the ten powers, their discipline does not wane. They engage in all the activities of vows, whatever they may be, And dedicate them to awakening for the benefit of all sentient beings.
examples.sa: शीलेन उद्गत भवन्ति समाधिकाङ्क्षी स्थित गोचरे दशबलान अखण्डशीलाः । यावन्ति संवरक्रिय अनुवर्तयन्ति तां सर्वसत्त्वहित बोधयि नामयन्ति ॥

examples.dm: If one wishes to attain the awakening of an Arhat or a Pratyekabuddha, One is immoral, unskilled, and one’s conduct has degenerated. But if one fully dedicates toward supreme, peaceful awakening, Even while engaged in sensory pleasures, one abides in the perfection of ethical discipline.
examples.gm: If one desires to touch the awakening of an arhat or solitary realizer, One's discipline is broken, one is unwise, and thus one's conduct degenerates. But if one completely dedicates it to the supreme, peaceful awakening, Even while engaged in sensory pleasures, one abides in the perfection of discipline.
examples.sa: सचि प्रत्ययानरहबोधि स्पृहां जनेति दुःशील भोति विदुषां तथ छिद्रचारी । अथ बोधि उत्तमशिवां परिणामयन्ति स्थितु शीलपारमित कामगुणेभि युक्तो ॥

examples.dm: The bodhisattva does not apprehend a prior limit, a later limit, Or a present; they are the purity of the three times. That which is such is unconditioned and free from conceptual elaboration; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Bodhisattvas do not apprehend the past limit, the future limit, And the present occurrence; the three times are pure. They are unconditioned and free from conceptual proliferation; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: पूर्वान्ततो न उपलभ्यति बोधिसत्त्वो अपरान्ततोऽपि प्रतिउपन्न त्रियध्वशुद्धो । यो शुद्ध सो अनभिसंस्कृतु निष्प्रपञ्चो एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who fully understands that all phenomena are non-conceptual, Empty, signless, and free from conceptual proliferation, Does not seek awakening through a dualistic wisdom; That yogi strives in the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whichever bodhisattva, non-conceptualizing, fully knows all dharmas As empty, signless, and free from elaboration, They do not seek awakening through dualistic wisdom; That yogin exerts themselves in the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व अविकल्पकु सर्वधर्मान् शून्यानिमित्त परिजानति निष्प्रपञ्चान् । न च प्रज्ञ बोधि परिएषति आशयेन सो युक्त प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय योगी ॥

examples.dm: The nature of all objective referents is boundless; Whatever the nature of sentient beings is, that too is boundless. The nature of the expanse of space is also boundless; The wisdom of the Knower of the World is also boundless.
examples.gm: The nature of objects of apprehension is boundless; Whatever the nature of sentient beings is, that too is boundless; The nature of the realm of space is also boundless; The wisdom of the Knower of the World is also boundless.
examples.sa: आरम्बणान प्रकृती स अ(न)न्तपारा सत्त्वान या च प्रकृती स अनन्तपारा । आकाशधातुप्रकृती स अनन्तपारा प्रज्ञा पि लोकविदुनां स अनन्तपारा ॥

examples.dm: However many sentient beings there are without exception throughout the three realms of existence, If one were to take all of them as a basis for consideration, and if all of them, To the Knowers of the World—the Buddhas, Arhats, and Pratyekabuddhas— Were to give gifts for infinite eons while seeking the excellence of a Śrāvaka,
examples.gm: However many sentient beings there are without exception in the three states of existence, Taking them fully into consideration, if all of them To the Knowers of the World, the Buddhas, Arhats, and Pratyekabuddhas Give gifts for infinite eons, and properly seek the śrāvaka path—
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व त्रिभवे निखिलेन अस्ति ते सर्वि दान ददयन्ति अनन्तकल्पान् । बुद्धानुलोकि विदु नार्हतिप्रत्ययानां यावन्ति श्रावकगुणान् परिकल्प स्थाने ॥

examples.dm: If, while dedicating, the notion of a mind arises, Or the notion of enlightenment, or the notion of sentient beings, Then because of such notions, one dwells in views and the mind is attached to the three; Because there is an object of observation, it is not a perfect dedication.
examples.gm: If, when dedicating, the notion of 'mind' arises, If there is the notion of awakening, the notion of dedicating, and the notion of sentient beings, Because of these notions, residing in views, the mind is attached to the three; Since there are apprehensions, it does not amount to dedication.
examples.sa: परिणामयन्तु यदि वर्तति चित्तसंज्ञा तथ बोधिसत्त्वपरिणामन सत्त्वसंज्ञा । संज्ञाय दृष्टिस्थितु चित्त त्रिसङ्गयुक्तो परिणामितं न भवती उपलभ्यमानम् ॥

examples.dm: They will desire honor and desire gain, And with a mind full of views, they will become intimate with householders; Abandoning the Dharma, they will engage in non-Dharmic activities— Leaving the path and wandering onto a wrong path, this is the work of Māra.
examples.gm: Desiring respect and desiring gain, With a mind full of views, they become intimate with families; Having forsaken the dharma, they will practice non-dharma activities; Having discarded the path, going on wrong paths—this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: सत्कारकाम भविष्यन्ति च लाभकामाः सापेक्षचित्त कुलसंस्तवसंप्रयुक्ताः । छोरित्व धर्म करिष्यन्ति अधर्मकार्यं पथ हित्व उत्पथगता इम मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: Those who have firm faith in the Sugatas and bodhisattvas, And whose intentions are focused on the supreme perfection of wisdom, Having completely transcended the two levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, May they swiftly attain the unassailable awakening of the Victors.
examples.gm: Whichever bodhisattva has firm faith in the Sugata, And applies their mind to the supreme perfection of wisdom, Having entirely transcended the two grounds of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, Will quickly attain the unconquerable enlightenment of the Victors.
examples.sa: यस्यामि श्रद्ध सुगते दृढ बोधिसत्त्वो वरप्रज्ञपारमित आशयसंप्रयोगो । अतिक्रम्य भूमिद्वय श्रावकप्रत्ययानां लघु प्राप्स्यते अनभिभू(तु) जिनान बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, although a bodhisattva may possess great faith, If they lack wisdom, they will quickly deteriorate. When faith is fully embraced by wisdom, They will transcend the two levels and attain supreme awakening.
examples.gm: Likewise, although a bodhisattva may have much faith, If they are completely lacking in wisdom, they will quickly become unfit. If their faith is fully embraced by wisdom, Having entirely transcended the two grounds, they will attain supreme enlightenment.
examples.sa: किंचापि श्रद्धबहुलो सिय बोधिसत्त्वो प्रज्ञाविहीन विलयं लघु प्रापुणाति । तं चैव श्रद्ध परिगृह्णयमान प्रज्ञा अतिक्रम्य बोधिद्वय प्राप्स्यति अग्रबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: A bird flying in the sky has no fixed station; It does not remain there, yet it does not fall to the ground. In this way, a bodhisattva who practices the gateways to liberation Does not touch upon nirvāṇa, yet does not engage with signs.
examples.gm: For a bird flying in the air, there is no place to abide; It does not abide there, nor does it fall to the ground. Likewise, a bodhisattva practicing in the doors of liberation Does not touch nirvāṇa and does not engage in signs.
examples.sa: पक्षिस्य नास्ति पदु गच्छत अन्तरीक्षे नो चापि तत्र स्थितु नो च पताति भूमौ । तथ बोधिसत्त्व चरमाणु विमोक्षद्वारे न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति नो च निमित्तचारी ॥

examples.dm: For example, just as the body of a magically conjured person is not invisible, And can be designated even by a name, Likewise, a bodhisattva who practices the doors of liberation Can be designated even by a name.
examples.gm: For example, just as an emanated human body is not invisible, And it can also be designated by a name; Likewise, a bodhisattva practicing in the doors of liberation Can also be designated by a name.
examples.sa: यथ निर्मितो पुरुष नो व अदृश्यकायो नामेन वा पुन स प्रज्ञपनाय शक्यः । तथ बोधिसत्त्व चरमाणु विमोक्षद्वारं नामेन वा पुन स प्रज्ञपनाय शक्यः ॥

examples.dm: When training, one does not make any claims about the training; One does not perceive a trainee or the qualities to be trained in, And does not conceptualize between training and non-training— Whoever trains in this way trains here in these Buddha-qualities.
examples.gm: When training, whoever does not assert any training, And does not observe the trainer or the dharmas of training, And does not conceptualize these two: having trained and not having trained, Whoever trains like that, trains in this Dharma of the Buddhas.
examples.sa: यो शिक्षमाणु न उपैति कहिंचि शिक्षां न च शिक्षकं लभति नापि च शिक्षधर्मान् । शिक्षा अशिक्ष उभयो अविकल्पमानो यो शिक्षते स इह शिक्षति बुद्धधर्मे ॥

examples.dm: When the Guides fully describe the trainings, This training is the supreme and unsurpassed among all trainings. Any wise person who wishes to reach the far shore of all trainings Should train in this Buddha-training, the Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: When the Guides fully proclaim this training, It is the supreme and unsurpassed of all trainings however many there are. Whichever wise one desires to go to the other shore of all trainings, Train in this perfection of wisdom, the training of the Buddhas!
examples.sa: यावन्ति शिक्ष परिदीपित नायकेन सर्वेष शिक्ष अयु अग्रु निरुत्तरा च । यः सर्वशिक्षविदु इच्छति पार गन्तुम् इमु प्रज्ञपारमित शिक्षति बुद्धशिक्षाम् ॥

examples.dm: Even if a bodhisattva indulges in the five objects of sensory desire, If they have gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And maintain the mental orientation toward omniscience, thinking, "I must achieve buddhahood," The wise should understand that they abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.
examples.gm: Even if a bodhisattva enjoys the five sensory pleasures, If they have taken refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And direct their mind toward omniscience, thinking, "I will accomplish buddhahood!" The wise one should be known as abiding in the perfection of discipline.
examples.sa: यदि पञ्च कामगुण भुञ्जति बोधिसत्त्वो बुद्धं च धर्म शरणागतु आर्यसंघम् । सर्वज्ञता च मनसी भविष्यामि बुद्धो स्थितु शीलपारमित वेदयितव्य विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: The eighth chapter: teaching the Dharmakāya. One fully embraces the pure realm and the purity of sentient beings; One fully embraces the lineage of the Buddha and the lineage of the Dharma; Likewise, one fully embraces the lineage of the Saṅgha and all phenomena.
examples.gm: Chapter Eight: Teaching the Dharmakāya. Fully upholds perfectly pure fields and pure sentient beings; Fully upholds the Buddha lineage and also the Dharma lineage; Likewise fully upholds the Sangha lineage and all dharmas.

examples.dm: Establishing the highest joy, respect, and faith, Having cleared away the obscurations of the afflictions and transcended all stains, Listen to this perfection of wisdom of the noble ones, who are dedicated to the welfare of beings, And to that which is the conduct of the heroic ones.
examples.gm: Having established supreme joy, respect, and faith, Having removed obscurations and afflictions and passed beyond stains, The perfection of wisdom of the gentle ones engaged in the benefit of beings, Listen to that in which the heroes practice.
examples.sa: पर प्रेम गौरव प्रसाद उपस्थपित्वा प्रजहित्व आवरण क्लेशमलातिक्रान्ताः । शृणुता जगार्थमभिप्रस्थित सुरव्रतानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति शूराः ॥

examples.dm: If one asks, "Why is this person called a 'bodhisattva'?" They seek the total exhaustion of all attachment, cutting through attachment. They touch the unattached awakening of the Victors; Therefore, they receive the name "bodhisattva."
examples.gm: Why are they called a "bodhisattva"? They sever attachment, desiring the exhaustion of attachment to all things. They contact the unattached awakening of the Jinas; Therefore, they obtain the name of "bodhisattva."
examples.sa: किं कारणं अयु प्रवुच्यति बोधिसत्त्वो सर्वत्र सङ्गक्रिय इच्छति सङ्गछेदी । बोधिं स्पृशिष्यति जिनान असङ्गभूतां तस्माद्धि नाम लभते अयु बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who practices in that way without doubt, Should be known as one endowed with wisdom, abiding in equanimity; Having fully understood that all phenomena are devoid of intrinsic nature, This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Any bodhisattva who practices in this way without doubt, Endowed with wisdom, should be known to abide in equality; Thoroughly knowing dharmas to be without nature, This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्तु न च काङ्क्षति बोधिसत्त्वो ज्ञातव्य यो विहर ते स उपायप्रज्ञो । प्रकृतीअसन्त परिजानयमान धर्मां एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: The Guide has proclaimed that perception is the near shore; By dismantling and abandoning perception, one goes to the far shore. Those who are free from perception have attained this subsequent state; Having crossed over, they abide by the Teacher’s command.
examples.gm: The Guide has proclaimed that perception is this shore; Destroying and abandoning perception, one goes to the other shore; Those who are free from perception, attaining this, Have reached the other shore and abide in the Teacher's word.
examples.sa: संज्ञेति नाम परिकीर्तितु नायकेन संज्ञां विभाविय प्रहाण व्रजन्ति पारम् । ये अत्र संज्ञविगमं अनुप्राप्नुवन्ति ते पारप्राप्त स्थित पारमिते हु भोन्ति ॥

examples.dm: On whichever path a universal monarch constantly travels, On that very path, the seven precious jewels and all the military hosts follow; Wherever this Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors goes, From that very place, all the qualities and dharmas will follow.
examples.gm: Whichever path a Universal Monarch always travels upon, By that very path, the seven precious things and all the troops proceed. Wherever this perfection of wisdom of the Victors goes, Along that very path, all qualities and dharmas will go.
examples.sa: येनैव राज व्रजते स ह चक्रवर्ती तेनैव सप्त रतना बलकाय सर्वे । येनैव प्रज्ञ इय पारमिता जिनानां तेनैव सर्वगुणधर्म समागमन्ति ॥

examples.dm: If no sprout exists, a tree could never grow in the world; In that case, how could branches, flowers, and fruit ever appear? If the mind of enlightenment did not exist, no Victors would ever arise in the world; And if so, how could the fruits—Indra, Brahmā, and the Hearers—ever appear?
examples.gm: If the emergence of a tree in the world never happens without a sprout, How could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits emerge on it? If the emergence of a Victor in the world does not exist without the mind of awakening, How could the fruits of Śakra, Brahmā, and śrāvakas emerge?
examples.sa: असतोऽङ्कुरस्य द्रुमसंभवु नास्ति लोके कुत शाखपत्रफलपुष्पौपादु तत्र । विन बोधिचित्त जिनसंभवु नास्ति लोके कुत शक्रब्रह्मफल श्रावकप्रादुभावः ॥

examples.dm: If one understands that these phenomena have ceased and are exhausted, And that which is dedicated is also exhausted, And that a phenomenon never dedicates to a phenomenon, Then by knowing in such a way, it is a perfect dedication.
examples.gm: If in this way one knows that this dharma has ceased and is exhausted, And that to which it is dedicated is also exhausted, And knows that a dharma is never dedicated to a dharma, Through knowing in that way, it is perfectly dedicated.
examples.sa: सचि एव जानति निरुध्यति क्षीणधर्मा तच्चैत क्षीण परिणामयिष्यन्ति यत्र । न च धर्म धर्मि परिणामयते कदाचित् परिणामितं भवति एव प्रजानमाने ॥

examples.dm: The third chapter teaches the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, the heroic practitioners Truly transcend the three realms, yet they do not enter a narrow liberation. Although they have eliminated the afflictions, they manifest birth; Although they are free from aging, sickness, and death, they manifest passing away.
examples.gm: The third chapter: teaching the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, wherever the hero practices, They completely transcend the three realms, yet are not liberated; Though afflictions are cleared away, they display birth; Though without aging, sickness, and death, they display death and transmigration.
examples.sa: त्रैधातुकं समतिक्रान्त न बोधिसत्त्वा क्लेशापनीत उपपत्ति निदर्शयन्ति । जरव्याधिमृत्युविगताश् च्युति दर्शयन्ति प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति धीराः ॥

examples.dm: Subhūti asked the Buddha, the Moon of Speakers: "What are the obstacles for those who delight in virtuous qualities?" The Teacher replied: "The obstacles that will arise are many; Of those, I shall briefly describe just a few."
examples.gm: Subhūti asked the Buddha, the moon among speakers: What are the obstacles for those who delight in qualities? The Teacher replied: There are many obstacles; Of those, I will fully explain just a few for now.
examples.sa: बुद्धं सुभूति परिपृच्छति वादिचन्द्रं क्यन्तन्तरायु भविष्यन्ति गुणे रतानाम् । बहु अन्तरायु भविष्यन्ति भणाति शास्त ततु अल्पमात्र परिकीर्तयिष्यामि तावत् ॥

examples.dm: All those who have passed, the current Protectors of the worlds of the ten directions, And those who will arise in the future, all emerge from her. She is the Mother who gives birth to the Victors, the teachers of the world, And she reveals the mental activities of other sentient beings.
examples.gm: Those protectors of the world in the past and in the ten directions, And those who will appear in future times, arise from this. She is the mother who gives birth to the Victors, the teachers of the world, And she reveals the mental conduct of other sentient beings.
examples.sa: येऽतीत येऽपि च दशद्दिशि लोकनाथा इतु ते प्रसूत भविष्यन्त्य् अनागताश् च । लोकस्य दर्शिक जनेत्रि जिनान माता परसत्त्वचित्तचरितान निदर्शिता(का) च ॥

examples.dm: Whoever sees in that way sees all phenomena. Just as a king remains impartial while his ministers perform all the tasks, Whatever activities of the Buddhas and teachings of the Śrāvakas there may be, The Perfection of Wisdom performs them all.
examples.gm: Whoever sees in that way sees all dharmas. Just as a king sits in equanimity while his ministers do everything, Whatever deeds of the Buddhas and dharmas of the śrāvakas there are, All of them are done by the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यो एव पश्यति स पश्यति सर्वधर्मान् सर्वान् अमात्यकिरिया ति उपेक्ष्य राजा । यावन्ति बुद्धक्रिय धर्मत श्रावकाणां प्रज्ञाय पारमित सर्व करोति तानि ॥

examples.dm: Those who practice in that way are the moons of speakers who live an excellent life; They are the refuge, the protector, and the dwelling place of beings. They are the support, the intellect, the island, and the guide for those seeking benefit, The illuminator, the lamp, the unshakeable speaker of the supreme Dharma.
examples.gm: Practicing thus, those oceans of goodness, moons of speech, Are the refuge, the defender, and the resting place of beings; They are the support, the mind, the island, and the supreme guides seeking their welfare; They are illuminating lamps, speakers of the supreme dharma, and are unperturbed.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्त गुणसागर वादिचन्द्राः त्राणा भवन्ति जगती शरणा च लेना । गति बुद्धि द्वीप परिणायक अर्थकामाः प्रद्योत उल्क वरधर्मकथी अक्षोभ्याः ॥

examples.dm: Whoever wishes to set forth in this Buddha vehicle Should train with an even mind toward all beings, the recognition of them as parents, A helpful attitude, and a loving heart, Being without harshness, remaining straightforward, and speaking gentle words.
examples.gm: Whoever desires to definitely emerge in this vehicle of the Buddha, With an even mind toward all beings, perceiving them as parents, Should act with an attitude of benefit and a mind of loving-kindness, Be free from rigidity, straightforward, and speak gentle words.
examples.sa: निर्यायनाय य इच्छति बुद्धज्ञाने समचित्त सर्वजगती पितृमातृसंज्ञा । हितचित्त मैत्रमन एव पराक्रमेय्या अखिलार्जवो मृदुगिराय पराक्रमेय्या ॥

examples.dm: They do not act as diviners, predicting whether those engaged in desire will have a boy or a girl. They strive in the supreme perfection of wisdom, which is utterly secluded, free from strife and contention, and their minds of loving-kindness are firm. Desiring omniscience, they are steadfast and possess a mind constantly dedicated to it.
examples.gm: They do not predict, saying, 'You will become a man or a woman engaged in actions of desire.' In the utterly isolated perfection of wisdom, they are free from conflict and dispute, and their mind of loving-kindness is firm. Desiring omniscience, they are steadfast and always endowed with a mind inclined toward it.
examples.sa: न च आदिशन्ति पुरुषैः स्त्रिय इच्छकर्मां प्रविविक्त प्रज्ञवरपारमिताभियुक्ताः । कलहाविवादविगता दृढमैत्रचित्ता सर्वज्ञकाम सद शासनि निम्नचित्ताः ॥

examples.dm: If, having thoroughly inquired about their conduct and faculties, The bodhisattva does not fully demonstrate the dharmas of emptiness and signlessness, Nor explain the dharmas of the irreversible stage, One should understand that such a person has not been prophesied.
examples.gm: If, when completely questioned about their practice and faculties, A bodhisattva, the dharmas of emptiness and signlessness Does not completely teach, and the dharmas of the irreversible stage Does not explain, they should be known as unprophesied.
examples.sa: यदि पृच्छमान चरि इन्द्रिय बोधिसत्त्वो गम्भीरधर्मपरिदीपन नो करोति । शून्यानिमित्त अविवर्तियबोधिधर्मां न च शोचती न च स व्याकृतु वेदितव्यो ॥

examples.dm: A bodhisattva who strives for the benefit of beings and has attained meditative concentration, Powers, faculties, liberations, and absorptions—if one treats them with contempt, Thinking, "This person does not practice in forest isolation," The Victor has declared that such a person dwells within the domain of Māra.
examples.gm: When a bodhisattva striving for the benefit of beings attains dhyāna, Powers, faculties, liberations, and samādhi, If one despises them, thinking, "This is not the conduct of isolated monasteries," The Victorious One says they abide in the domain of Māra.
examples.sa: सो चंक्रमार्थम् अभियुक्तकबोधिसत्त्वान् बलध्यान-इन्द्रियविमोक्षसमाधिप्राप्तान् । अभिमन्यते न इमि रण्यविवेकचारी न विवेकगोचरु अयं हि जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: It is taught that the way one grasps is the way one is completely afflicted; It is said that when "I" and "mine" are not observed, there is total purification. In this, without anything being defiled or purified, The Bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Just as there is apprehension, so is complete affliction taught; Not apprehending self and what belongs to self is taught as complete purification; In this, without anything becoming afflicted or completely pure, The bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यथ उद्ग्रहो तथ प्रकाशितु संकिलेशो व्योदान उक्त अहु मह्य अनोपलब्धि । न हि अत्र कश्चि यो क्लिश्यति शुध्यते वा प्रज्ञाय पारमित बुध्यति बोधिसत्त्वे ॥

examples.dm: However, when those wise ones possess intense resolve, And day and night look toward the supreme meaning of the perfection of wisdom, At that time, their body, mind, and speech move like a bird in the sky; How could the factions of darkness ever find an opportunity against them?
examples.gm: When those wise ones, possessing intense resolve, Behold the supreme meaning of the perfection of wisdom day and night, At that time, their body, mind, and speech move like a bird in the sky; How could the associates of the dark one find an opportunity?
examples.sa: यथ ते भवन्ति विदु आशयसंप्रयुक्ता दिवरात्रि प्रज्ञवरपारमितार्थदर्शी । तद कायचित्त खगपक्षिसतुल्यभूता अवतारु सो कुतु लभिष्यति कृष्णबन्धुः ॥

examples.dm: In this way, the wise light-makers train in wisdom; They do not give rise to even a single unvirtuous thought. Just as darkness cannot remain in the space before it When it is overwhelmed by the rays of the sun moving through the sky,
examples.gm: The wise light-makers train in wisdom like that; They do not generate even a single non-virtuous mind. Just as, when outshone by the rays of the sun moving in the sky, Darkness does not remain in the space before it.
examples.sa: शिक्षन्तु एव विदु प्रज्ञ प्रभंकराणां नोत्पद्यते अकुशलमपि एकचित्तम् । सूर्ये यथा गगनि गच्छति अन्तरीक्षे रश्मीगते न स्थिहते पुरतोऽन्धकारम् ॥

examples.dm: Just as the element of space and that space itself do not conflict, And it does not exist as something to be attained by anyone at all, Likewise, the bodhisattva who is skilled in the practice of wisdom Is like space, and practices in a state of total peace.
examples.gm: That realm of space and what contradicts that space Do not exist, and no one has attained them; Likewise, the wise bodhisattvas practicing wisdom Are like space and practice total peace.
examples.sa: आकाशधातु गगनस्य सिया विरोधो न हि तेन तस्य कुतु केनचिदेष प्राप्ता । एमेव प्रज्ञचरितो विदु बोधिसत्त्वो अभ्योवकाशसदृशो उपशान्तचारी ॥

examples.dm: Though birds dwell in the sky, they do not fall; Though fish dwell in the water, they do not suffocate or die. Likewise, through the power of meditative concentration, Bodhisattvas Who have reached the far shore dwell in emptiness but do not pass into nirvāṇa.
examples.gm: A bird dwells in the sky, yet does not fall; A fish dwells in water, yet does not suffocate and die; Likewise, the bodhisattva, by the powers of concentration, Having reached the other shore, dwells in emptiness and does not pass into nirvāṇa.
examples.sa: आकाशि पक्षि विहराति न चो पताति दकमध्यि मत्स्य विहराति न चो मराति । एमेव ध्यानबलपारगु बोधिसत्त्वो शून्याविहारि न च निर्वृति प्रापुणाति ॥

examples.dm: Those who have attained supreme wisdom and abide in the meditative concentrations Also experience the four sublime formless meditative stabilizations. These concentrations are beneficial for supreme and sublime awakening; Yet, a bodhisattva does not train in them for the sake of exhausting the outflows.
examples.gm: Those who have attained supreme wisdom and abide in the dhyānas, Also experience the four holy formless samādhis; These dhyānas are beneficial for supreme holy awakening, But the bodhisattva does not train to exhaust the defilements.
examples.sa: ध्याने स्थितोऽत्र भवती वरप्रज्ञलाभी आरूप्यरूपि च समाधि चतस्र श्रेष्ठा । उपकारिभूत इमि ध्यान वराग्रबोधौ न पुनास्रवक्षति स शिक्षति बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: If a bodhisattva, while dwelling in meditative absorption and concentration, Should generate a mind that desires the vehicle of the Arhats or Pratyekabuddhas, They have become uncomposed, agitated, and mentally distracted; The Buddha's qualities are completely lost, like a ferryman whose boat has been wrecked.
examples.gm: If a bodhisattva abides in the samādhis of the dhyānas, But generates a mind desiring the vehicle of an arhat or pratyekabuddha, They are not in meditative equipoise, but agitated and their mind is distracted; The qualities of a Buddha completely diminish, like a boatman whose boat breaks.
examples.sa: यदि बोधिसत्त्व विहराति समाधिध्याने रहप्रत्ययानि स्पृहबुद्धि न संजनेय्या । असमाहितो भवति उद्धतक्षिप्तचित्तो परिहीनबुद्धिगुण नाविक भिन्ननावो ॥

examples.dm: If, with the thought, "I shall bring all beings to maturity and act for their benefit," One applies oneself with body, speech, and mind, Yet remains dwelling in the perception of a self, one has become lazy; They are as far from omniscience as the earth is from the sky.
examples.gm: Thinking, "Having completely ripened beings, I will act for their benefit," If they exert themselves with body, speech, and mind, Because they abide in the perception of a self, they have become lazy, And they become as far from omniscience as the sky is from the earth.
examples.sa: सचि कायचित्तवचसा च पराक्रमेय्या परिपाचयित्व जगती करिष्यामि अर्थम् । कौसीद्यप्राप्त भवती स्थितु आत्मसंज्ञैः नैरात्मभावनविदूरि नभं व भूमेः ॥

examples.dm: One who practices patience should also cultivate this thought: "In the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama, there is much suffering. Since I have helplessly experienced harm due to the causes of sensual desire, Why should I not now endure hardship for the sake of enlightenment?"
examples.gm: The one who practices patience should also generate the mind thinking this: "In the hells, animal realms, and the world of Yama, there is much suffering; If one experiences unavoidable harm as a result of sensory pleasures, Why should I not now practice patience for the sake of awakening?"
examples.sa: क्षममाणु एव पुन चित्त उपादितव्यो नरकेषु तिर्ययमलोकि अनेक दुःखा । अनुभूय कामगुणहेतु अकामकारा कस्मा हु अद्य न क्षमेय निदान बोधौ ॥

examples.dm: Having realized that all phenomena are by nature selfless and insubstantial, If they can give away even their own flesh without a discouraged mind, Then at that time, what need is there to mention the giving of external objects? If they were to be stingy, it would be impossible.
examples.gm: Knowing that all dharmas are by nature selfless and insubstantial, If they give away even their own flesh without a shrinking mind, Then what need is there to mention giving away external objects? For them to act with miserliness is impossible.
examples.sa: ज्ञात्वा च धर्मप्रकृतीं वशिका निरात्म्यं आत्मान मांस त्यजमानु अदीनचित्तो । प्रागेव वस्तु तद बाहिर नात्यजेया अस्थानमेत यदि मत्सरि सो करेया ॥

examples.dm: Yet a wise bodhisattva with skillful means Were to rejoice in the substance of those meritorious deeds, And fully dedicate it toward supreme, sublime enlightenment for the sake of sentient beings, By that complete dedication, one will outshine all living beings.
examples.gm: Whatever wise bodhisattva, skilled in means, Rejoices in their bases of meritorious actions, And fully dedicates them to supreme awakening for the sake of beings, By fully dedicating them, they outshine all beings.
examples.sa: यश् चो उपायकुशलो विदु बोधिसत्त्वो तेषां स पुण्यक्रियवस्त्वनुमोदयित्वा । सत्त्वार्थ अग्रवरबोधयि नामयेया अभिभोति सर्वजगती परिणामयुक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Through wisdom, one thoroughly understands the nature of phenomena, And will perfectly transcend the three realms without exception. Having turned the precious wheel, that preeminent leader among men Teaches the Dharma to beings in order to bring suffering to an end.
examples.gm: By wisdom, having fully known the nature of phenomena, One will completely transcend the three realms without exception; The supreme leader of humans, having turned the precious wheel, Teaches the Dharma to beings in order to exhaust suffering.
examples.sa: प्रज्ञाय धर्मप्रकृती परिजानयित्वा त्रैधातुकान्त समतिक्रमते अपायान् । वर्तित्व चक्ररतनं पुरुषर्षभाणां देशेति धर्म जगती दुखसंक्षयाये ॥
